business_scope.primary_industry_name: Delivery-Only Multi-Brand Cloud Kitchen Facility Operations

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid — Quebec private law is civil-law, while criminal, federal, and trade/customs law is common-law statutory; commercial registration follows Quebec civil and administrative rules.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada–United States–Mexico Agreement (CUSMA), including investment chapter
Canada–European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA), including investment chapter
Canada–United States Tax Convention (1980), as amended

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA) and PCMLTF Regulations SOR/2002-184; Criminal Code, R.S.C. 1985, c. C-46; An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; Regulation respecting the application of that Act, CQLR c P-44.1, r. 1; Civil Code of Québec, CQLR c CCQ-1991, arts. 2236–2252 (limited partnership regime).
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal — limited-partner identities and individual UBO details are maintained in the partnership records and are disclosed to FINTRAC, tax authorities, and qualified financial institutions/payout platforms on lawful request; the public REQ extract identifies only the general partner(s) and the registered establishment.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Status / Certificate of Good Standing for each non-resident corporate general partner or corporate limited partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original corporate registry of the jurisdiction of incorporation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized true copy of passport / national identity card for each individual general partner and each individual UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport/identity issuing authority in the holder's country of nationality

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized/certified French translation of the foreign-language limited partnership agreement, articles of the corporate GP, and any foreign-language UBO declarations
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: OCCQ-licensed certified translator (Ordre des traducteurs, terminologues et interprètes agréés du Québec), with apostilled source documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Residence/proof-of-address (dated within 90 days) and tax residency certificate of each individual general partner / UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank, utility, municipal authority, or national tax administration in the country of residence

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: At formation and before any capital commitment, every general partner, limited partner, and beneficial owner (25% threshold) must be screened against: OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, Canada's sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2017, c. 21, and the Criminal Code corruption/offence-proceeds provisions. PEP definitions and enhanced due diligence follow PCMLTFA s. 9.3 and Part 4 of the PCMLTF Regulations, including foreign PEPs, domestic PEPs, and heads of international organizations, with beneficiary family/close-associate controls. Source-of-funds, source-of-wealth, and ongoing transaction monitoring documentation is mandatory for non-resident contributors and any high-risk jurisdiction nexus.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) — official online enterprise register and name-reservation service (https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name must be in French under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11. Non-Latin scripts must be transliterated into Latin characters; a foreign trademark may keep its original form only if recognized as an exception or accompanied by a French descriptive element. The word element must include the French legal designation 'société en commandite' or its abbreviation 'S.E.C.'; an English-only 'Limited Partnership' suffix is not acceptable for REQ registration.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names suggesting Crown, governmental, or public regulatory authority: 'Québec', 'Canada', 'Provincial', 'Municipal', 'Regie', 'Royal', 'Crown' — require prior ministerial or Registraire authorization

Regulated-industry or reserved professional tokens: 'Bank', 'Trust', 'Insurance', 'Broker', 'Lawyer', 'Notary', 'Accountant', 'Auditor', 'Engineer', 'Architect', 'University' — require prior sector regulator approval
Words that are obscene, misleading, contrary to public order, or likely to create confusion with a recorded enterprise or trademark
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A REQ name reservation may be requested online before filing the LP declaration and is valid for 90 days, renewable once by filing before expiry. If REQ refuses the name, the filer receives a reasoned refusal notice. An internal review request may be filed with the Directeur du Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the refusal, attaching the original name search, a revised French-compliant proposed name, and any trademark/title authorization; if the internal review is adverse, an appeal to the Court of Québec may be filed within 30 days of the review decision.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Allowed for the administrative registered office, provided the address in Quebec is a physical service address where legal notices may be served and records can be produced; a pure post-office box or virtual-mail drop is not sufficient. For a ghost kitchen, a separate physical licensed commercial kitchen facility must exist in Quebec; the REQ-registered establishment should correspond to that operational address or to a reliable administrative service address, and no customer-facing retail presence is required.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Registered-office annual probability of unannounced inspection is low (about 2–5%). The active ghost-kitchen operating site faces high inspection risk (greater than 50% in year one) for municipal food-safety, fire-safety, health, and zoning spot checks; FINTRAC compliance examinations may additionally occur on an RBA basis if the LP serves as an AML reporting entity in the delivery/aggregator channel.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec, CQLR c CCQ-1991, arts. 2186-2235 and 2236-2249 governing partnerships and limited partnerships; Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, particularly ss. 21-25 concerning registration and disclosure.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), administered by the Québec Ministry of Employment and Social Solidarity.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Declaration of Registration (Déclaration d'immatriculation) for a limited partnership, filed through the Québec Enterprise Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital or mandatory escrow account applies to a Québec limited partnership. Capital contributions and contribution timing must be specified in the limited partnership agreement. A designated Québec financial institution account may be opened after registration; any bank-required deposit is contractual and is not a statutory escrow requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The board of directors of the corporate general partner resolves that the general partner shall execute the limited partnership agreement and subscribe for its agreed general-partner interest, and shall procure all agreed limited-partner subscriptions. The registered office of the limited partnership is approved at [Québec address]. [Name] is appointed authorized representative and [Name] secretary for registration, banking, tax, licensing, and contracting matters. The officers are authorized to file the Declaration of Registration with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec, obtain required tax accounts, open bank and payment accounts, and apply for all food, municipal, fire, occupational, and environmental approvals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Approve the partnership structure and name
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online services and Québec Enterprise Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Select a compliant French or bilingual name, verify availability and prohibited terms, identify at least one general partner and the limited partners, and execute a written limited partnership agreement. The limited partnership must maintain a Québec address for its principal establishment or registered office. Notarization is not generally required for the partnership agreement, but powers of attorney and foreign corporate records should be notarized or certified where required by the receiving institution.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name and name-availability evidence
Names, addresses, and status of general and limited partners
Québec principal establishment or registered-office address
Corporate authority documents for any corporate partner
Certified French translations for documents not available in French where required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, submit an amended name or use the assigned Québec enterprise number with a compliant declared name. If ownership or address information is queried, file corrected disclosure and supporting authority documents.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Declaration of Registration for a limited partnership, disclose the prescribed partners and representatives, state the principal establishment, describe the activities, and pay the applicable Québec fee in Canadian dollars. Upload or retain supporting documents as required. The filing is an administrative registration rather than incorporation of a separate legal person; the partnership is formed by agreement under the Civil Code of Québec.
required_dossiers: Limited partnership agreement or confirmation that it is executed
Business activity description, including delivery-only food preparation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond through the REQ portal within the stated correction period, amend incomplete or inconsistent entries, provide requested evidence, and resubmit with any additional fee. An administrative review or judicial remedy may be considered for a disputed refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency Business Registration Online and Revenu Québec online services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the Québec enterprise number, obtain the Canada Revenue Agency business number and register applicable GST/HST, payroll, and import or export accounts. Register for Québec QST and source deductions with Revenu Québec where thresholds or activities require registration. Determine whether the partnership must file a Québec partnership information return and maintain partner allocation records.
required_dossiers: Tax residence and beneficial ownership information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct registration data through the applicable tax portal, submit missing authorization forms, and request an account review or written determination where registration status is disputed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ), Food Establishment Permit application service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before commencing food preparation or sale, apply for the MAPAQ permit category applicable to preparation and sale of food for human consumption. Identify every kitchen location, food activity, operator, and responsible manager. Submit the application, premises information, menu or process description, lease or occupancy evidence, and fee. Do not rely solely on delivery-platform registration as regulatory authorization.
required_dossiers: Premises address and lease or occupancy evidence
Menu, food processes, and operating schedule
Food safety training evidence for responsible personnel
Site plan and equipment layout where requested
Waste, grease, refrigeration, and sanitation procedures
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to MAPAQ deficiencies, arrange a corrective inspection, and submit amended plans or procedures. Do not operate until the permit is issued or MAPAQ confirms that the activity is exempt.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure municipal zoning, building, and occupancy approvals
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality or borough responsible for the kitchen premises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Confirm that the zoning designation permits commercial food preparation, delivery-only operations, ventilation equipment, loading, waste storage, and customer-free operations. Obtain construction, alteration, signage, plumbing, electrical, ventilation, grease-interceptor, and occupancy permits as applicable. Obtain written landlord consent where the lease restricts cooking, exhaust, odors, or commercial equipment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Submit revised plans, seek a minor exemption or zoning variance where legally available, attend municipal inspection, and correct deficiencies before occupancy or operation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete fire, occupational, and environmental compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal fire service, Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST), and Québec Ministry of the Environment, the Fight Against Climate Change, Wildlife and Parks
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain fire-prevention acceptance for cooking equipment, suppression systems, exits, alarms, emergency lighting, and occupant load. Complete CNESST employer registration and workplace prevention measures. Confirm whether an authorization under section 22 of the Environment Quality Act is required for wastewater, emissions, hazardous materials, or equipment changes. Establish grease, used-oil, food-waste, refrigerant, and chemical handling controls.
required_dossiers: Fire prevention inspection or acceptance record
CNESST employer registration and prevention program
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inspection findings, obtain reinspection, file required environmental authorization applications, and appeal or request review of an agency decision within the applicable statutory period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Agriculture, des Pêcheries et de l'Alimentation du Québec (MAPAQ); municipal authorities also regulate zoning, building, occupancy, plumbing, ventilation, and fire matters.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: MAPAQ Food Establishment Permit (Permis d'exploitation d'un établissement alimentaire), for preparation and sale of food for human consumption.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (Québec Ministry of the Environment, the Fight Against Climate Change, Wildlife and Parks)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Normally exempt from a full Environmental Impact Assessment for an ordinary delivery-only commercial kitchen. A prior authorization under section 22 of the Environment Quality Act may nevertheless be required for specified wastewater, atmospheric emissions, hazardous substances, construction, or industrial equipment activities.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Comply with municipal sewer bylaws and any applicable authorization conditions for pH, fats, oils, grease, suspended solids, temperature, and prohibited substances. Install and maintain grease interception where required. Control cooking odors, particulate matter, VOCs, refrigerants, and exhaust through approved equipment. Store chemicals and wastes securely; use authorized contractors for used oil, food waste, hazardous waste, and refrigerant recovery. No single province-wide restaurant VOC limit should be assumed without site-specific review.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Obtain municipal fire-service acceptance for hood suppression, extinguishers, alarms, exits, emergency lighting, occupancy load, and fire separations. Obtain building, plumbing, electrical, ventilation, and structural approvals where construction or equipment loads require them. Register as an employer with CNESST, implement worker training and hazard controls, maintain safe food and chemical handling procedures, and complete required inspections and certifications before opening.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Federal: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — portal: CRA My Business Account at canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/e-services-businesses/business-account.html. Quebec: Revenu Québec — portal: Mon dossier d'entreprise / CléInfo at revenuquebec.ca.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Quebec limited partnership begins by filing its déclaration de société en commandite with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) to obtain the Quebec enterprise number (NEQ). The general partner then applies to the Canada Revenue Agency using Form RC1 (Request for a Business Number and selected program accounts, principally RT for GST/HST) to obtain the federal Business Number (BN); the partnership itself is the registrant and indirect-tax person. Next, the partnership registers for QST with Revenu Québec using the business registration application (formerly LM-1) and is issued a QST registration number. There is no statutory minimum capital requirement for the limited partnership, and non-resident individuals or entities may own limited-partner interests without any direct registration obligation unless individual Canadian/Quebec tax returns are triggered. All tax accounts must be updated within prescribed statutory time limits and records must be kept in French-acceptable auditable form.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible; for Canadian and Quebec income tax purposes, the limited partnership (société en commandite) is fiscally transparent and its income or loss flows through to the general and limited partners. However, for GST/HST and QST purposes, the limited partnership is treated as a separate registrant and is responsible for collecting, reporting, and remitting indirect tax on taxable supplies made in Quebec.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election is available under Canadian or Quebec domestic tax law; the pass-through classification is automatic for a genuine limited partnership. For U.S. federal tax purposes, the Canadian limited partnership may be classified under U.S. check-the-box rules (Treas. Reg. §301.7701-3), but any such U.S. election does not alter Canadian/Quebec treatment. Canada also applies anti-hybrid mismatch rules under the Income Tax Act and the Quebec Taxation Act that may deny benefits or re-characterise payments where a foreign jurisdiction treats the partnership as opaque; these are statutory constraints, not elective classification mechanisms.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Canada/Quebec consumption taxes: federal Goods and Services Tax (GST/TPS) at 5% and Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) at 9.975%, combined effective headline rate of 14.975% on taxable supplies made in Quebec. The Harmonized Sales Tax (HST) does not apply in Quebec.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 in taxable supplies made in Canada/Quebec during the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters or in any single calendar quarter, excluding certain capital-property sales and with related-person aggregation rules. Once a supplier ceases to be a 'small supplier' and is carrying on business in Canada/Quebec, registration with the CRA for GST and with Revenu Québec for QST is mandatory, generally within 30 days. A non-resident-owned ghost kitchen must monitor platform-sourced gross considerations to stay compliant.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada and Quebec do not operate a continuous-transaction-control, real-time tax clearance, mandatory e-invoice API, or digital-stamping regime. Electronic invoicing is permitted provided it is legible, accurate, contains prescribed GST/HST and QST information, and is retained for six years. Quebec rules require French-language commercial documents where provided to customers. Payment-rail files from UberEats and DoorDash and platform settlement statements are not substitute fiscal invoices and must be reconciled to issued invoices and general ledger records.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating is available only for genuine exports: goods exported from Canada in accordance with the Customs Act by the supplier or for the supplier, or services supplied to a non-resident where the service is performed wholly or substantially outside Canada and the Canadian/Quebec consumption benefits do not attach. For an ISIC 5610 ghost-kitchen business, prepared meals delivered to Quebec consumers are taxable supplies and cannot be zero-rated merely because payment is remitted through UberEats or DoorDash. Cross-border kitchen-capacity or intangible services to a non-resident brand may qualify for zero-rating only if all performable services occur outside Canada and supporting records demonstrate the non-resident recipient and lack of Canadian use.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA Customs Export Declaration or Canadian Export Reporting System output
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing export from Canada and foreign destination
Proof of export and statutory declaration where the carrier is not a licensed CBSA reporting entity
Inward Remittance Certificate or equivalent upstream banking record proving payment from the non-resident customer
Contracts, service-delivery logs, kitchen-utilisation records, and revenue-allocation memoranda substantiating the zero-rated portion
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec apply heightened audit scrutiny to zero-rating claims. If export documentation is missing, contradicted by business reality, or fraudulent, the supplier is reassessed for uncollected GST at 5% and QST at 9.975% on the full consideration, plus retroactive interest. Gross negligence penalties can be 50% of the tax sought to be evaded; criminal tax evasion under the Excise Tax Act carries fines between 50% and 200% of the evaded tax and imprisonment. Equivalent Quebec penalties apply under the Tax Administration Act, and input tax credits or input tax refunds are clawed back proportionately to the denied zero-rating.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), in coordination with the Department of Finance Canada for sanctions and administrative capital controls; FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) enforces cross-border EFT monitoring under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA); OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) supervises federally chartered banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Fully liberalised. The Canadian dollar is a free-floating, freely convertible currency under IMF Article VIII, with no exchange controls, no surrender requirements, and no prior approval mechanism for current-account or capital-account transactions. Capital proceeds, profit distributions, and trade settlements can be converted and remitted without central-bank authorisation. Practical frictions are limited to: (i) FINTRAC reporting for any cross-border transfer exceeding CAD 10,000; (ii) Part XIII federal and Quebec provincial withholding tax on non-resident limited-partner distributions (25% statutory, treaty-reduced); and (iii) a mandatory Investment Canada Act notification to ISED for the establishment of the new Canadian enterprise, while review thresholds (CAD 1.075 billion for WTO investors) are far above the proposed vehicle size.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender or mandatory conversion regime exists in Canada. Export proceeds and foreign-currency settlement inflows may be held, repatriated, or converted at the treasury's discretion without timeline constraint. For the ghost kitchen, UberEats and DoorDash payouts settle in CAD via domestic direct-deposit rails; foreign-source trade revenue may be retained in USD or any convertible currency, subject only to CRA record-keeping, QST/HST reconciliation, and the fintech platforms' internal payout policies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Desjardins Group (Fédération des caisses Desjardins du Québec)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low as a primary custody treasury; Medium as a supplementary payout rail. Canada does not issue EMI (Electronic Money Institution) licenses. Cross-border fintechs (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Airwallex) operate as FINTRAC-registered Money Services Businesses, not as deposit-taking institutions under the Bank Act, and therefore cannot offer CDIC-insured operational deposits. Their UBO and sector-risk models frequently reject ISIC 5610 aggregator settlement profiles. Recommended use: low-value foreign supplier disbursements only, held on a zero-balance pass-through basis.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a Quebec LP with a non-resident limited partner holding >25% equity, a physical in-branch interview is effectively mandatory for the initial Capital Escrow Account: National Bank, RBC, and BMO require at least one signatory (or the General Partner director) to appear at a Montreal, Toronto, or Vancouver flagship branch before activation. Publicly traded banks allow a notarised remote-opening package only where the GP is Canadian-controlled and all partners hold Canadian-issued identity documents. Practical mandate: schedule a single 48-hour presence visit in week 1 of onboarding; reserve 5-10 business days for post-interview compliance release.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident LP UBO holds >25% and resides in a FATF grey-listed or sanctions-affected jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports of all natural-person UBOs; apostilled Certificate of Good Standing; home-jurisdiction tax residency certificate; sworn source-of-funds affidavit; signed LP agreement with capital-commitment schedule; undertaking that no crypto or sanctions nexus exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sector-risk flag: ISIC 5610/NAICS 722513 ghost kitchen receiving high-frequency micro-settlements from DoorDash/UberEats, which Compliance may misinterpret as money-service-transmission or layering activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed DoorDash/UberEats merchant agreements in the legal name of the LP; platform payout policy schedules; monthly statement-to-invoice reconciliation mapping every settlement EFT to an underlying food-order transaction; QST/GST/HST registration certificate; Quebec municipal hospitality-operating licence; food-safety permit.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection documented only as a loan or hybrid, causing recharacterisation as shareholder debt and triggering Part XIII withholding plus thin-capitalisation review under the Income Tax Act.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital-contribution memorandum; CPA-prepared capital-account ledger; partnership deed including contribution release clause; GP board resolution declaring non-refundable equity character; document set confirming no interest coupon, no fixed maturity, and no redemption feature.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) status of a foreign-resident limited partner or GP director.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCMLTFA s.11.1 beneficial-ownership declaration; PEP risk-acceptance questionnaire signed by the bank's AML officer; police clearance certificate from the PEP's residential jurisdiction; wealth-origin attestation from a licensed legal or accounting advisor.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound capital via SWIFT MT103 with field 70 remittance narrative reading 'Capital contribution to Quebec limited partnership - direct investment, non-recourse'. Provide the receiving bank's SWIFT BIC (e.g., ROYCCAT2 for RBC), the LP's 12-digit account number, 5-digit transit, and 3-digit institution number (Canada does not use IBAN). Attach the covenant file (LP agreement, REQ enterprise registration excerpt, partnership certificate) for the correspondent bank's economic-sanctions and FX-control due diligence. Transactions above CAD 10,000 trigger FINTRAC CEFT reporting and an enhanced due-diligence call-back; funds typically remain in the escrow sub-ledger for 2-5 banking days pending verification before release into the operational capital account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Domestic platform payouts and supplier payments settle via the Payments Canada ACSS EFT rail; the LP must register valid institution-transit-account routing data with UberEats and DoorDash direct-deposit portals. Cross-border trade settlements (foodstuffs, packaging, kitchen equipment) use SWIFT MT103 through Payments Canada LVTS for open-account payables; documentary shipments against title require irrevocable Commercial Letters of Credit (MT700/MT707) issued under UCP600 at the trade desks of BMO, RBC, or National Bank. USD-denominated disbursements are executed either through the bank's dedicated US-dollar non-resident account or a secondary USD operating account, with conversion executed at the bank's institutional spot desk and documented for CRA transfer-pricing and Quebec sales-tax audit trail.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: CAD/USD and CAD/EUR deliverable FX forwards (10 business days to 12 months) under ISDA 1992 or CSA master agreements with OSFI-regulated Schedule I bank counterparties
CAD/USD FX swaps and swap-points trades settled through LVTS for rolling working-capital hedging

Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (XCS) for the intercompany debt facility from a non-resident parent, designated for hedge accounting under IAS 39/IFRS 9 with full collateral and credit-support documentation

NDFs (non-deliverable forwards) are generally unavailable and discouraged for a fully convertible currency such as CAD; any offshore quote would carry premium pricing and is outside the approved treasury policy for this LP

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Update Declaration (déclaration de mise à jour annuelle)...
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), Ministère de la Justice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary month rule: must be filed during the calendar month corresponding to the month of initial LP registration (e.g., registration on 15-March-2025 ⇒ filing window from 01-March to 31-March of every subsequent year).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing after the anniversary month triggers a CAD 42 late surcharge and a REQ default notice. Failure to file within 60 days of the notice results in a strike-off declaration and statutory dissolution of the LP (Civil Code of Québec, art. 2256), terminating the limited-liability protection of limited partners.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Partnership Information Return (T5013) including T5013 Statement of Partnership Income slips for each partner of the limited partnership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 5 months after the LP's fiscal year-end; if the fiscal period ends on 31-December and all partners are residents of Canada, the filing due date is extended to 30-June of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No late-filing penalty for partnerships with five or fewer partners. For partnerships with six or more partners, ITA subsection 162(7) imposes CAD 25 per partner per month of delay, up to a maximum of 12 months; parallel Revenu Québec penalties may apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Quebec limited partnership is not statutorily required to obtain an independent audit solely because of entity form. Compulsory audit arises when (i) the LP is a reporting issuer or publicly accountable enterprise as defined by CPA Canada Handbook Section 2001; (ii) the partnership agreement, a lender, or a delivery-platform commercial agreement mandates audited financial statements; or (iii) the corporate general partner is a CBCA/Quebec Business Corporations Act corporation that must appoint an auditor. In the absence of these factors, a review engagement or compilation is accepted market practice.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Private limited partnerships apply Canadian ASPE (CPA Canada Handbook Part II) as the default framework; IFRS (Part I) applies to publicly accountable LPs and may be required by the partnership agreement. Financial records must also satisfy the books-and-records rules of the Quebec Tax Administration Act and the Information Tax Act for platform payout reconciliation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of all general and limited partners is integrated into the REQ annual update declaration; the declaration must re-state partner names, addresses, contributions, and the general partner's authority. A transfer of any partnership interest requires a separate declaration of modification submitted to REQ within 30 days of the transfer (CAD 42 fee). No standalone federal UBO annual return applies to a partnership; beneficial-ownership transparency is achieved through REQ public disclosure of partners and through CRA access to the partnership's books; if a CBCA-incorporated general partner exists, its separate beneficial-ownership register obligations under the new federal UBO regime apply.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Not applicable at entity level (Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent). Federal general corporate rate: 15%; Quebec provincial general rate: 11.5%. Combined non-incentivized federal/provincial corporate rate: 26.5%. Active business income of a Canadian-controlled private corporation (not applicable to LP) may qualify for federal small business deduction and Quebec reduced rate, but partnership allocations flow through to partners.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No statutory tax holiday applies to the LP itself. Eligible expenditures may qualify for Investment Tax Credits (federal and Quebec), Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) credits, and Quebec's refundable tax credit for E-commerce and Digital Transformation. The ghost kitchen operator may claim Canada Employment Credit? No—employment credits are limited. Capital cost allowance (CCA) on kitchen equipment, leasehold improvements, and digital platforms may reduce taxable income. Provincial Quebec innovation credits: C3 (tax credit for the development of e-business) may provide up to 30% refundable credit on eligible employee wages, capped.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Federal: T5013 (Statement of Partnership Income) filed via the Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) GST/HST NETFILE or approved third-party E-file. Provincial Quebec: TP-600 (Quebec Partnership Information Return) filed via Revenu Québec's electronic service 'transmission électronique' (EDIFACT) or approved software. Each partner also files their own T1/T2/TN/TP-1/TP-3 depending on residence and status.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (fiscal year-end normally December 31 for Canadian LPs; permitted non-calendar fiscal year only if all partners consent and business is seasonal or custom; CRA may require calendar year for tax shelter partnerships). Quarterly instalments of corporate tax are not required for the LP itself since no entity-level tax. Partners file annual returns; withholding remittances (payroll, GST/HST) are made quarterly or monthly.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: T5013: On or before the last day of the fifth month after the partnership's fiscal year-end (e.g., March 31 for December 31 year-end) but no later than March 31 if a T3/T5/T5013 is required. TP-600: On or before the last day of the sixth month after the fiscal year-end (e.g., June 30 for December 31) for partnerships with all partners resident in Quebec; if any non-resident partner, the deadline is the last day of the sixth month for federal? Actually TP-600 deadline aligns with the federal requirement? Revenu Québec requires filing no later than the last day of the sixth month after fiscal year-end (June 30 for calendar year). Partners’ forms: T1 due April 30; T2 due six months after tax year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue from all ghost kitchen virtual brand sales, delivery provider settlements (UberEats, DoorDash), and ancillary income, net of cancellations and refunds. Report in Canadian dollars.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a limited partner resident outside Canada, report only the Canadian-source business income allocated to that partner in Canadian dollars. Attach a T5 or T5013 slip to the partner. Non-resident partners must file T1 or TN return if income from carrying on a business in Canada. Stop any Part XIII withholding on marketing or management fees paid to non-residents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 – Box 103: Cost of Goods Sold (Restaurant Inventory)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct food and beverage costs, packaging, and kitchen supplies consumed in delivery-only menus. Standard inventory accounting, including beginning/ending inventory.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No specific non-resident adjustment; ensure expenses are apportioned to permanent establishment activities. Non-resident partners cannot deduct expenses without a direct connection to Canadian-source business income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 – Box 145: Wages, Salaries, and Benefits (Non-Management)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total compensation paid to kitchen staff, prep cooks, delivery coordinators, and administrators, excluding owner-managers, including contributions to pension plans and employment benefits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If a non-resident partner renders services to the partnership, ensure arm's-length compensation reflected. Wages paid to Canadian employees are not deductible for non-resident partner's Canadian-source income unless incurred through a permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Office rent, software automation licenses, customer service, accounting and legal fees, bank charges, and payment processor fees (UberEats/DoorDash commissions). Must be properly documented.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate administrative expenses using a reasonable basis to Canadian-source income. Non-resident partners cannot claim head-office or headquarter allocations from a foreign parent unless substantiated by a cost-sharing or service agreement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 – Box 202: Current-Year Partnership Active Business Income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net income or loss from the ghost kitchen business determined under Canadian tax rules, after adding back non-deductible items and applying specific tax adjustments (CCA, meals/entertainment (50%), non-deductible penalties).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident limited partner, report only the share of income attributable to a Canadian permanent establishment. If the LP is not in Canada and the partner is a non-resident, they may be exempt from Canadian tax under Article VII of the Canada–U.S. Treaty or similar. File the appropriate treaty claim with waiver of 25% withholding on distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: TP-600 – Section 1: Identification and Partner Information
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: LP name, business number (BN), Quebec establishment number (NEQ), fiscal year-end, legal address, and complete list of partners with percentages, addresses, and residency status. For each partner, provide Quebec provincial allocation factor (percentage of commercial activities in Quebec).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose each non-resident limited partner's legal name, jurisdiction of residence, and Ontario/Quebec allocation percentage. For U.S. LLC partners, provide the owning member's identity. Indicate whether any partner is a 'specified non-member' under Quebec's anti-avoidance rules for partnerships.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quebec-source gross revenue of the partnership, including delivery platform sales attributable to customers in Quebec, and any other income earned in Quebec. Exclude inter-provincial sales not attributable to Quebec.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident partner, Quebec taxation only applies if the partnership's Canadian-source income is allocated to Quebec activities based on the partner's share. Provide a formulaic apportionment or specific identification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible expenses incurred in Canada and Quebec for the ghost kitchen, including inventory, employee wages in Quebec, rent for Quebec premises, delivery apps' fees, and Quebec portion of insurance and marketing. Follow CRA and Revenu Québec common adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must respect the 'base erosion' provisions – no deduction for amounts paid to non-arm's-length non-residents unless charged and substantiated under Quebec's transfer-pricing rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: TP-600 – Lines 9-11: Allocation of Profit/Loss to Partners
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Assign each partner's share of ordinary business income, capital gains, and other income according to the partnership agreement (generally profits/distributions only if the LP has two or more classes of units). For fiscal transparency, the LP does not pay Quebec tax; each partner reports their allocated share.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the non-resident partner's share in the Province Quebéc column only for business income attributable to Quebec permanent establishment. If the non-resident partner has no permanent establishment in Canada, the allocated income is generally not taxable in Canada, but the TP-600 must still report it for informational exchange purposes.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: T5013 – Box 503: Gross Rental Income (if any)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: If the ghost kitchen LP subleases any space or equipment to third-party virtual brands, report rental revenue separately. Not expected for a delivery-only operator, but include if charging rent to a partner-owned entity.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident lessors must file a Part XIII election to report Canadian rental income on net basis. For an LP with a non-resident partner, ensure no deemed dividend on payments to partners in excess of business income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Federal T5013 late filing: $25 per day up to $2,500, plus an additional penalty of $100 to $1,000 if the form is not filed within 30 days of the due date. For partnerships with more than 100 partners, the penalty increases. Incorrect/unresolved forms: penalties for knowingly false statements up to $100 for each slip. Quebec TP-600 late filing: $25 per day up to $2,500, plus interest; failure to provide partner's information may lead to a $100 penalty per partner. Revenu Québec may impose a 5% penalty on the balance of tax payable by the partnership (if any deemed tax) plus interest. Criminal penalties for wilful evasion: on summary conviction, a fine not exceeding $5,000 and/or imprisonment not exceeding two years; on indictment, a fine up to $10,000 and/or imprisonment up to five years.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Canada's Part XIII gross withholding tax on dividends paid by a Canadian corporation to a non-resident is 25%. However, an LP is not a corporation; profit distributions to partners are not dividends. When a Canada-resident LP allocates active business income to a non-resident limited partner, the distribution itself is typically a return of capital or profit; no Part XIII withholding applies because the partnership is transparent and the income is taxable to the partner as Canadian-source business income. If the LP pays management fees, interest, royalties, or rental consideration to a non-resident, the payor must withhold 25% Part XIII tax unless reduced by treaty. Quebec also imposes a 15% withholding on distributions to non-residents from a Quebec partnership if the LP has elected to be a 'non-resident-owned investment corporation'? No such election – Quebec has no separate Quebec WHT on non-resident distributions to partners; the federal Part XIII regime applies to certain passive payments. For treaty relief: a non-resident partner can file a Part XIII waiver with CRA by obtaining a treaty-based determination (e.g., Form NR301 for U.S. residents) or by filing a Canadian tax return to claim a refund. The effective treaty rate on Canadian business profits of a non-resident is zero if no permanent establishment (Canada–U.S. Article VII). For dividends sourced from a deemed Canadian subsidiary, treaty reduces the 25% rate to 5% for corporate shareholders holding at least 10% voting stock, or 15% otherwise (Article X of Canada–U.S. Tax Treaty). Since an LP is pass-through, the 'dividend withholding' concept applies only if the LP is a central cash-management vehicle that makes taxable deemed-dividend distributions under subsection 15(1) of the Income Tax Act. Practical guidance: route profit distributions as current-account draws; do not characterize them as dividends or royalties in the partnership agreement.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: 1. Confirm the non-resident partner's country has an income tax treaty with Canada (e.g., U.S., U.K., France). 2. Obtain a valid Certificate of Residence (e.g., IRS Form 6166, HMRC Form A1, or the relevant QR code for EU) from the partner's tax authority, issued within the last three years. 3. Attach the certificate to an NR301 waiver form (for business income, royalties, management fees) or an NR302/NR303 for Part XIII tax on amounts paid to non-residents. 4. File the waiver with CRA before the payment is remitted to avoid withholding; if already withheld, the partner can file a T1/T2 and claim a refund using T7B. 5. For Quebec: Revenu Québec uses the same federal treaty criteria but requires a separate certificate of residence (RCV-2) for relief from provincial withholding on payments to non-residents; however, Quebec does not impose a separate distribution WHT. 6. Maintain a contemporaneous file containing the treaty position, TRC, analysis under Article VII (business profits) or Article X (dividends), and evidence of no permanent establishment in Canada (e.g., no fixed place of business in Quebec, no dependent agent closing contracts).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory Part XIII rate for interest paid to a non-resident at arm's length is 0% (participating interest paid to non-residents is subject to 25%); royalties for use of patents, trademarks, or know-how are subject to 25% Part XIII unless reduced. Treaty: Canada–U.S. – interest 0% (except on participing debt), copyright royalties for software or literary works 0%, other royalties 10% (Canada–U.S. Article XII – industrial royalties 10%, literary/artistic 0%). Canada–U.K. – interest 0% for arm's length, royalties 10% (industrial) and 0% for literary? Actually the general treaty royalty rate is 0% for lists. Quebec follows federal treaty allocations. For ghost kitchen virtual brands, trademark royalties to a U.S. parent or brand owner will attract 25% Canadian WHT unless reduced to 10% via treaty; interest on intercompany loans – if the loan is arm's length interest at market rate, the 0% treaty rate applies, but the lender must be the beneficial owner. Quebec imposes a 12% provincial tax on interest payable to non-residents if the debt is secured by Quebec real property or a Quebec partnership? No – Quebec's provincial WHT on interest is 0% for arm's length and 15% for non-arm's length if it is a debt in Quebec? Section 1015 of the Taxation Act – Quebec requires withholding of 15% on non-arm's length interest payments to non-residents. For the LP, payments of management fees to a non-resident partner (a separate legal person) are subject to 25% federal Part XIII (unless treaty reduces to 0% for business profits under Article VII) and Quebec 15% withholding if not attributable to a Quebec permanent establishment. Revenu Québec TP-600 schedule states no provincial withholding for partnership distributions, but Quebec does require a 15% withholding on payments to non-residents for services rendered in Quebec, which may apply to tech fees for software Big Data.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Canadian dollar; under CRA's Transfer Pricing Memorandum (TPM-16), the requirement to prepare contemporaneous documentation (Master File and Local File) is triggered when the aggregate value of cross-border transactions with non-residents exceeds CAD 1 million in a fiscal year for goods/services, CAD 100,000 for patents and intangibles, CAD 100,000 for interest, and CAD 100,000 for management fees (threshold depends on transaction type). For a Quebec LP operating ghost kitchens, if it pays royalties or delivery-platform fees to a non-Canadian affiliate (e.g., a U.S. parent brand licensor) exceeding CAD 1 million, a Country-by-Country Report is required only if the consolidated group revenue exceeds CAD 1 billion for the previous fiscal year. Quebec's provincial Administrative Guideline ARQ.25.2.5 requires a Local File for intra-group transactions if the gross revenue of the Quebec partnership exceeds CAD 100,000 and the partner is non-resident? Use the federal threshold for prudential compliance: prepare a TP questionnaire and benchmarking study if any transaction exceeds CAD 200,000 per category.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: Quebec also accepts the 'substantially similar' method – e.g., Berry Ratio for distribution/service businesses
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Canada has not enacted a specific Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) like the UAE or EU ATAD. However, federal general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) under Income Tax Act section 245 denies the benefit of a transaction if the primary purpose is avoidance and it is not real actual economic substance. Quebec has a similar GAAR under section 1029.6 of the Taxation Act. The CRA has expressly targeted partnerships used to park intangible assets in low-tax jurisdictions. A Ghost Kitchen LP with no physical location, no employees in Canada, but generating significant revenues through delivery platforms will be subject to the 'permanent establishment' test and the substance-over-form doctrine. Additionally, Quebec imposes an annual $1,000 to $3,000 licence fee for 'restaurant operations' that requires a real location. The LP must demonstrate: (1) actual management operations conducted in Quebec; (2) genuine decision makers with physical offices; (3) tangible kitchen equipment and inventory; (4) valid employment contracts with Canadian staff; and (5) a business plan and board minutes (for corporate partners) reflecting economic activity. The CRA's 'specified non-resident' anti-deferral rules (section 75(2)) can reattribute partnership income to the contributor of property if a person or partnership contributes property to a partnership on condition that income may revert to them – a scenario common in virtual brand licensing.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willfully failing to report delivery platform income (UberEats/DoorDash), inflating deductions, or misclassifying inventory as operating expenses. Concealing the existence of a Quebec permanent establishment to avoid Canadian income tax. Underreporting sales to reduce Part XIII withholding on distributions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Federal: Income Tax Act section 238 – summons default penalties: for each offence, a fine of CAD 1,000 to CAD 25,000 and/or imprisonment up to 12 months. On conviction of evasion (s. 239): a fine of 50% to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded or imprisonment not exceeding two years (summary) or up to five years (indictment). Quebec: Taxation Act section 1050 – penalies of 50% of unpaid tax, plus a fine not exceeding CAD 10,000 and imprisonment not exceeding two years for wilful evasion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a corporate partner of the LP are jointly and severally liable for unpaid GST/HST and payroll withholding (source deductions) if they knew, or reasonably should have known, of non-remittance. For tax evasion, criminal liability may attach to persons who 'directly, or through omission or commission, participated in the illegal act' – including officers and directors who authorized the evasion. Civil restitution: directors are liable for the full amount of unpaid taxes, interest, penalties, and may be subject to a court order to restore property to the partnership if illegal distributions are made. Travel bans and asset freezes may be issued under the Income Tax Act s. 226(1) if the taxpayer is attempting to leave Canada without paying assessed taxes. Imprisonment is possible for evasion under the Criminal Code (conspiracy or fraud) up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying all revenue to a foreign virtual brand owner (e.g., a Delaware LLC) as trademark royalty, guaranteeing that the Quebec LP earns zero or minimal profit, while the foreign owner has no active business or employees. Applying a low royalty rate inconsistent with the royalties' economic value. Failing to file a T5013 or TP-600 with the foreign partner's allocation in order to hide the treaty exemption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA may re-determine the arm's-length price under s. 247(2), increasing the LP's taxable income by the re-priced royalty, applying 10% interest, and a transfer-pricing penalty up to 10% of the net downward adjustment (s. 247(3)). The penalty applies if the taxpayer failed to make reasonable efforts to determine arm's-length terms. Quebec assesses an additional 10% penalty under the Taxation Act s. 1064.2. Searches and prosecutions may follow if false documents are submitted.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the Canadian partner that signed intercompany agreements can be held liable for the TP penalty if they signed a return they knew was incorrect (negligence). The liability is limited to fines of CAD 5,000 to 10,000 for failure to file TP documentation (s. 247(7)). Civil liability: a director who authorizes a royalty payment that drains a partnership may be sued for creditor claims; in bankruptcy, the court may impose a 5-year travel ban for non-cooperation in examinations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a Quebec Limited Partnership as a mail-drop with no employees, no bank account in Quebec, no physical kitchen, and no operational control, used solely to receive delivery-platform payments before transferring 99.9% of the profit to a non-resident partner. Declaring all risks to the non-resident and no Canadian source tax. Failing to obtain a restaurant operation permit from the Revenu Québec or municipal licence in Montréal, QC, for a delivery-only kitchen.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CRA can disregard the partnership arrangement under section 75(2), attributing income directly to the non-resident, then assessing a 25% Part XIII withholding on distributions or 45% deemed dividend for a 'designated partnership' under s. 16(1.1) of the ITAR. Revenu Québec may impose a fine of CAD 5,000 to CAD 50,000 for operating a restaurant without a valid permit under the Loi sur la protection du consommateur and the Régie des alcools, des courses et des jeux (RACJ) – even if no alcohol, a food services establishment permit is required. Corporate law sanction: the enterprises register may be revoked; the LP loses limited liability protection for partners if no registered head office (Quebec Business Corporations Act, though LP registrations are under the Quebec Civil Code art. 2236).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: If the court pierces the partnership veil (partnership is not a separate legal person), general partners face unlimited liability for the partnership's debts for all approved operations. Directors of a corporate general partner may be liable for the full unpaid taxes under the Quebec Taxation Act s. 23.1 if the corporation is a vehicle of a fraud. A criminal charge under the Criminal Code for fraud (s. 380) carries a maximum imprisonment of 14 years. Travel bans are routinely issued if the director is a foreign national with non-Canadian assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing delivery payments through personal bank accounts or using crypto wallets not linked to the registered LP. Failing to register with FINTRAC as a 'food processing and retailing' business? Actually ghost kitchens are not AML reporting institutions unless they also function as payment service providers. Intentional violation: providing false information to UberEats on beneficial ownership, or receiving cash on delivery and laundering it without recording sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, a food operator is not a reporting entity unless it issues or redeems money orders. Correct trigger: not an AML violation for the kitchen itself, but if the LP systematically handles large amounts of cash (not normal for delivery) without proper books, the CRA can invoke the 'gross negligence' penalty of 50% of concealed income. FINTRAC may be involved if the LP collaborates with a payment service provider to break transactions under CAD 10,000. Criminal sanction for aiding laundering: up to 10 years imprisonment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are not automatically liable, but if they personally approve opening multiple corporate bank accounts with the sole purpose of avoiding reporting thresholds, they can be charged with money laundering (Criminal Code s. 462.31). Civil confiscation of the profits from the ghost kitchen operation is possible. A travel ban can be imposed by the court under mutual legal assistance requests if the director attempts to flee Quebec to a non-extradition country.
